ledger.note: 24 February 1538: the Treaty of Nagyvárad gives the Habsburgs Royal Hungary. 'Zápolya conceded Ferdinand's rule over western Hungary (Royal Hungary)'; the Royal Hungary page: 'Temporary territorial division between the rival rulers John I and Ferdinand I occurred only in 1538'; Pressburg became 'the new capital' when the division took effect. The Royal Hungary page dates the state from 1526 (two crowned kings after Mohács); the page that dates the land is 1538.

ledger.note: 1595: 'Mansfeld's Christian forces captured Esztergom and Visegrád on the Danube'. The page does not say how long they were held; the Great Turkish War page has Esztergom surrendering to the Holy League again in 1683.
1596: 'Ottomans conquered Eger' (Mezőkeresztes, 24-26 October 1596). The page does not say which side held Eger; as a frontier fortress behind the Habsburg line it is read as royal.

ledger.note: 1598: 'Habsburg forces retook Győr and Komárom'.

1600: the Ottoman Kanije eyalet is set up around Nagykanizsa ('Kanije (1600)'); the Long Turkish War page has the Habsburg siege of Nagykanizsa failing in 1601 and the Ottomans 'kept Eger and Kanizsa' in 1606. The capture itself is not dated on a page opened.
11 November 1606: Zsitvatorok. The Habsburgs 'Received Vác, which the Ottomans had held since 1541'.

region.text: the frontier fortresses of Veszprém, Győr, Komárom, Esztergom, Székesfehérvár and Eger

ledger.note: 11 November 1606: Zsitvatorok ends the Long Turkish War; 'The war was indecisive, with little territory changing hands'.
1663: the Austro-Turkish War reaches Slovakia: the Ottoman army 'in September conquered the town of' Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky).
September 1663: Nové Zámky (Érsekújvár) falls to the Ottomans.
10 August 1664: the Peace of Vasvár; the Habsburgs recognise Ottoman control of 'Transylvania, Nagyvárad, and Érsekújvár'.

region.text: Ottoman Hungary, the front of the Great Turkish War

ledger.note: 1683: the Great Turkish War; the Ottomans 'laid siege to Vienna on 14 July 1683'. The first Hungarian ground changing hands is Esztergom, after Párkány, in October 1683.
October 1683: 'Victory at Párkány in October 1683 led to Esztergom surrendering after a short siege.'

1685: 'Eperies, Kaschau and Tokaj fell soon afterwards. The Imperial forces took these towns.' The page does not say who held them; the counterpart is my reading (Thököly's Upper Hungary, a Cliopatria row for 1683-1686), to be checked.
19 August 1685: 'Érsekújvár (Nové Zámky) fell on 19 August' to the imperial forces.
2 September 1686: Buda is retaken after 78 days; it had been Ottoman since 1541.

1687-1691: bridging. 'Turkish resistance then collapsed across the region'; Mohács (1687) 'a crushing defeat for the Sultan'; Slankamen (August 1691) 'secured Habsburg possession of Hungary and Transylvania'. The page names no town; the region is my reading (all of the Ottoman Hungary except the Temeşvar eyalet).

wars.name: Hungarian succession war between Ferdinand I and John Zápolya
wars.outcome: The country 'was ruled by two crowned kings' after Mohács; the Treaty of Nagyvárad of 24 February 1538 gave the Habsburgs western Hungary.
wars.note: Named by me; the kingdom dossiers carry the contest 1528-1538. No territory zone is given because no page opened names the holdings before 1538.

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: Indecisive: the Ottomans kept Eger and Kanizsa, the Habsburgs got Vác; peace of Zsitvatorok on 11 November 1606; Bocskai rose in 1604-1606.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663-1664)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans took Nové Zámky in September 1663 and kept it at Vasvár on 10 August 1664.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Holy League takes Esztergom (1683), Nové Zámky (1685), Buda (2 September 1686); Slankamen (1691); Karlowitz in January 1699.

certainty.note: The division line was a chain of fortresses, not a surveyed boundary; the treaties of 1606 and 1664 name fortresses (Vác, Eger, Kanizsa, Nové Zámky).

notes:
Royal Hungary is a state Cliopatria lacks (the scope of eu-15 asks for royal versus Ottoman Hungary as a divided state). Starts 1538, the date a page gives for the division (24 February, Nagyvárad); the Royal Hungary article itself runs 1526-1867. It overlaps the habsburg-monarchy dossier, which gains the same land in 1547 and holds it to 1699; the colour agent should decide whether royal-hungary is drawn as the Hungarian crown inside the Habsburg colour or instead of it. Ends 1699: the later kingdom (1699-1867) is the Habsburg monarchy's, and a dossier for it would need pages on 1699-1867 that this budget did not reach.

Not settled: (1) the extent in 1538-1593: the pages say 'the northern and western parts of the country', 'present-day Slovakia and northwestern Transdanubia'; the counties are my reading, and the Croatian crown lands (Habsburg from 1527 per the Kingdom of Hungary dossier) are not included: a 'Croatia under the Habsburgs' dossier is needed (see croatia-in-union-with-hungary notes). (2) Esztergom/Visegrád (gained 1595) were Ottoman again by 1683 (Great Turkish War page): the date of that loss is on no page opened, and the keyframes drop them in 1606 as a bridging step; no loss event is booked. (3) Eger's holder before 1596 is not on the page. (4) The 1685 gain of Eperies, Kaschau and Tokaj has its counterpart (principality-of-upper-hungary) by reading. (5) The Bocskai principality (Prince of Hungary at Szerencs, 17 April 1605) holds land in northeast Hungary that no page opened names. (6) The 1687 gain is a bridging reading at confidence 1. Page budget 5-6; the Budin Eyalet page is shared with ottoman-hungary.
